Its own settling test resolved against the code: line 1007 is extension = "." + file_path.rsplit(".",1)[-1] — a plain suffix lookup. Canonical `Dockerfile` yields "" and never reaches the ".dockerfile" entry.
Header tuple is (header, node.start_point[0]+1, members[0].start_point[0], ...). First member on the definition's own line gives end_line = start_line - 1. Inverted range.
_subdivide emits header (node.start_byte..members[0].start_byte) plus each member's own byte range. Inter-member gaps and everything after members[-1].end_byte are in no chunk.

SPAN uses (?<!`) twice in a module-scope regex literal, so an engine without lookbehind fails to parse the module, not the function. Its own settling test — the configured build targets — resolves in its favour: vite.config.ts sets no build.target and package.json has no browserslist, so the default baseline (well below Safari 16.4) applies. Severity honestly pitched at info.

No page param, per_page<=100, GitHub returns oldest-first — so a >100-commit PR yields the oldest 100. Second half verified too: api/reviews.py:355-377 leaves seen_boundary False when head_sha is absent from the page and the fallback then marks every returned commit is_new.

scope is None unless len(review_diffs) < len(file_diffs), so a selection touching every file persists no commits key. Its subtler half also holds: _diffs_to_review's docstring states every failure path falls back to the full diff, so keying scope off commit_shas alone would be wrong.
